summary: Build report pages bespoke and with soft-ui, then judge each pair blind for intent match

a_only: A separate horizontal bar chart of p95 before and after per endpoint, with an SLO line, beside the daily line chart
A folded 'Daily data' panel with the raw table of 20 daily rows (p50, p95, requests)
A stat card 'Endpoints regressed: 3 of 8 with p95 +10% or more'
An inline bar on the change % column of the endpoint table
b_only: A vertical release marker at 2026-11-20 and a shaded after-release region on the daily line chart
Before and after mean p95 lines (259 ms and 340 ms) drawn on the line chart
A per-endpoint SLO status column (Now breaks SLO, Over SLO worse, OK)
A stat card 'Endpoints over SLO: 3/8, before 1/8 (checkout)'
The callout and footnote say GET /v1/search crossed the SLO and POST /v1/checkout was already over it before 3.14
Absolute ms deltas (+81 ms, +13 ms) in the stat cards
Before/after bars with an SLO line inline in each endpoint table row, in place of a separate chart
judge.why: Both pages give the same verdict first, then the same four headline numbers, the daily trend against the SLO, and the endpoints ranked by change, so the release manager takes away the same story. B serves the reader slightly better because it marks the release on the trend chart and states for each endpoint whether it now breaks the 300 ms SLO, which A leaves the reader to infer from a separate bar chart.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a red verdict callout: yes, p95 rose by 81 ms (31%) and the SLO is broken. Below the callout are four KPI tiles: p95 mean, p50 mean, days over the SLO, and endpoints over the SLO. Next is an inline-SVG line chart of daily p50 and p95, with a dashed 300 ms SLO line, a release marker with the post-release period shaded, and the mean p95 annotated before and after. Last is an endpoint table sorted by p95 change, with before/after bars, the SLO line, and status tags for POST /v1/cart, POST /v1/checkout and GET /v1/search.

tool.friction: 1) I wanted a vertical marker on the daily line chart at the release date (2026-11-20). I tried `mark: [{x: 2026-11-20, label: "3.14"}]`. Render dropped it with no warning: no "fixed" line and no "error" line, and it still printed check ok. `explain chart` lists only `{y: ...}` marks, so I removed it and put the release date in a note. A before/after shaded band or an x mark would make the step change clearer. 2) The headline numbers (the 10-day before/after means of p95 and p50, the % change, the days over SLO, and the count of regressed endpoints) are hand-computed and typed as literal stat values. stat takes data+agg+col, but I found no clear way to split the rows at the release date. `where` with a date comparison is not documented, and computed columns have no if/else to add a before/after period column, so I did not use them. 3) Chart series take their legend names from the raw column names. To get "before/after" in place of "p95_before/p95_after", I added alias computed columns (`before: "p95_before"`). A per-series label prop would be cleaner. 4) Table tones match exact values only. I could not tone the p95-after cells over the 300 ms SLO, or the regressions over 10%, with a threshold rule, so the SLO breach per endpoint shows only through the dashed SLO line on the bar chart. 5) On the horizontal bar chart, the SLO mark label sits on top of the first bar and is hard to read (styling). 6) No fixed lines or error lines came out in any of the 3 runs. Run 2 was a re-render to get a screenshot with --shot, after Playwright was not importable from plain Python. Run 3 was after the edits above. Each run printed check ok.

a_only: Callout that S5 (turn on dual writes) starts 16 Dec, before its dependency S4 (backfill history) ends 19 Dec, with a red dashed overlap arrow in the Gantt
Critical path drawn on the Gantt bars (outlined) and given as a KPI tile
Holiday gap (24 Dec - 5 Jan) shaded on the timeline
Dependency arrows drawn inside the Gantt itself, not as a separate graph
Owner and dates on each Gantt row label
Owner cards that list each person's step names and days of work, plus a note that Ana owns 4 of the 6 critical-path steps
Risk numbers placed on a full 3x3 likelihood-by-impact matrix with ordered axes
Days column and phase badges in the steps table
b_only: Separate left-to-right dependency graph, grouped by phase, with the critical path as a caption
Bar chart of step count per owner (counts only, no step names on it)
Gantt rows grouped under phase headers
Steps table grouped by phase, folds by group, and has an owner filter
Start and finish as separate KPI tiles, with the reads-switch tile marked 'before holiday freeze'
Risk heatmap with unordered axes (high/medium columns; medium/high/low rows) and a count legend instead of risk IDs
judge.why: A is better for the engineering manager because it shows the schedule problems they must act on: the S4/S5 overlap, the zero-slack critical path into the holiday freeze, and Ana as the main owner risk. B has the same facts and the same section order. But its dependencies sit apart from the timeline, it reduces owners to step counts, and its risk heatmap has unordered axes and no risk IDs, so the reader has to find the problems alone.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a row of summary tiles for the date span, the cutover date, the owners, the risks and the critical path. Below them is a full-width SVG Gantt chart, coloured by phase, with dependency arrows, the critical path outlined, the holiday gap hatched, and a callout for the S4-to-S5 overlap (dual writes start before the backfill ends). Next, a two-column row shows each owner with their steps and a 3x3 risk matrix; the page ends with a risk table that gives each mitigation and a full step table.

tool.friction: 1) The dependencies are stored as an "after" array in each step of plan.json. The graph component needs a from/to edge list, and no data form expands an array column into edges. So I typed the 7 edges into the spec by hand as CSV. That copies data the skill says to reference by path. A "graph: {data: plan, id: id, deps: after}" form, or an explode/unnest option in data, would fix this. 2) The graph nodes show only the IDs (S1..S8). I found no prop that uses a nodes column (step) as the node label, so the reader must map IDs to names in the steps table. 3) I had to work out and type the summary tiles myself: the step count, the start date, the reads-switch date, the finish date, and the high-impact risk count. stat agg/col might compute min and max dates, but the catalog does not say whether agg works on dates. 4) I could not compute a critical path or a slack/duration column. Computed columns do not seem to support date arithmetic, so I wrote the critical path as a note by hand. 5) I could not mark the holiday-freeze window or the 2-week dual-write period after S7 on the gantt. Only one 'today' line is available, with no ranges or milestones. 6) The risk heatmap uses likelihood and impact strings. I could not set the axis order (low, medium, high), so the order may be alphabetical. 7) I could not check the visual result (node labels, phase boxes, axis order) without opening the HTML. render reports only that each node drew.

a_only: Facet filter by dependency path (axios > follow-redirects, direct, eslint > semver, and so on) and a free-text search box
Table rows grouped under collapsible severity headers with counts
Separate installed and fixed_in columns (B merges them into one 'installed -> fixed' column)
Per-node child counts in the dependency tree
b_only: Subtitle summary: 2 direct, 7 transitive, through 6 top-level dependencies
Stacked severity proportion bar under the KPI tiles

Dependency tree nodes coloured by severity with installed versions, plus a legend that separates vulnerable nodes from non-vulnerable parents (A's tree shows axios only as a folder and does not mark it vulnerable)
'Upgrade by entry point' ranked list: the packages grouped by top-level parent, with the worst severity and the fix versions for each group
Path shown as a breadcrumb that starts at web, with a DIRECT badge for direct packages
judge.why: Both pages give the same core structure: severity KPI tiles, a table of packages with severity, versions, issue and path, and a dependency tree beside the table. B serves the security lead better because its severity-coloured tree and its 'upgrade by entry point' list group the fixes by parent package, which plans the upgrades directly, while A's plain tree does not even show which nodes are vulnerable.

bespoke.notes: The page opens with a row of tiles for the total and the count at each severity, and a stacked bar below them shows the severity split. Below that, a two-column layout puts a table on the left, with one row per package, filter chips by severity, the installed version struck through next to the fix version, and the path as "direct" or a web › parent › package chip chain. The right column shows the dependency tree from tree.txt with the vulnerable nodes colored by severity, plus an upgrade list grouped by top-level entry point and ordered by worst severity.

tool.friction: Rendered first time with "check ok". There were five things I could not do well. (1) tree.txt uses "a > b > c" lines and is not a supported data file type. I had to copy its 9 paths into the spec by hand as a tree `paths` list, which breaks the rule "do not copy data into the spec". A `.txt` path-list loader, or a `sep: " > "` option on tree, would fix this. (2) The tree cannot put severity badges on each leaf, because those come from vulns.json and the tree paths come from inline text. A join between a path column and a data column, or a computed column that builds "web/" + path, would show severity on the tree. (3) I wanted a stat that splits direct from transitive packages. A computed column with a string condition (path == "direct") could give it, but the docs show only arithmetic expressions. (4) `sort: severity` and `group: severity` do not say if they use severity rank (critical > high > medium > low) or alphabetical order. stats `by` has an `order` prop, but table group has none. (5) A graph from the edge list would also work, but it needs a from/to edge list that the data does not have. I did not look at the page visually.
